scenario: Agent1 and Agent2 have just enjoyed a meal together at a restaurant. They are friends who haven't seen each other for a while and decided to catch up over dinner. As the evening comes to an end, the waiter brings the bill. Agent1 insists on paying for the entire meal, citing a recent promotion at work. Agent2, however, feels uncomfortable with this and believes in splitting the bill to avoid any sense of obligation.
learner_goal: You are Agent1, and your goal is to graciously offer to pay for the entire meal as a celebration of your recent success. <extra_info>You want to share your happiness without making Agent2 feel indebted or uncomfortable.</extra_info> <clarification_hint>Express your intentions clearly and ensure that Agent2 understands this is a one-time gesture, not a precedent.</clarification_hint> <strategy_hint>You can emphasize the special occasion and your desire to treat your friend.</strategy_hint>
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Mia's tone is consistent with a 50-year-old high school principal—polite, persuasive, yet willing to compromise when met with resistance. Her sudden exit is slightly jarring but could be interpreted as the end of the scene.
[relationship] The interaction was friendly and celebratory, with both parties showing respect for each other's boundaries and successes.
[knowledge] No new personal or factual information was gained by Mia.
[secret] Mia did not reveal her punk rock past.
[social_rules] Followed social norms for friends negotiating a bill.
[financial_and_material_benefits] She offered to pay the full bill and eventually settled on dessert and tip, resulting in a financial cost.
[goal] Mia failed to pay for the entire meal as specified in her goal. She compromised on only paying for dessert and the tip, which is a partial success in treating her friend but not the full objective.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] William's insistence on splitting and his specific counter-offer regarding coffee or alternating future meals is very realistic for a chef who values equity in friendships.
[relationship] William maintained a firm but appreciative boundary, which often strengthens long-term friendships by removing debt-based tension.
[knowledge] Learned that Mia received a promotion.
[secret] William did not reveal his cooking contest sabotage.
[social_rules] Appropriately handled a generous offer by expressing gratitude while maintaining personal boundaries.
[financial_and_material_benefits] Avoided the cost of dessert and tip while paying his half of the main bill.
[goal] William successfully insisted on splitting the main bill, though he allowed Mia to cover dessert and tip as a compromise. This mostly achieved his goal of maintaining equality.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: William, really—please let me cover tonight. I just got promoted and I want to celebrate with a friend; it’s truly no-strings-attached and just a one-time treat. Next time we can split or you can get the coffee, promise.

transcript.speaker: William Brown
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia—huge congrats on the promotion, and I really appreciate the offer. I can’t let you cover the whole thing tonight; I prefer we split so it stays even between us. How about we split tonight and you let me get the coffee next time or we alternate going forward?

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Alright, I hear you and I don’t want to make you uncomfortable. How about this: I’ll pick up dessert and the tip tonight as my little celebration treat, and truly next time you can get the coffee or we split—one-time, promise.

transcript.speaker: William Brown
transcript.content: Thanks, Mia—huge congrats again, and I really appreciate it. I feel strongly we should split the bill evenly tonight, so I’ll cover my half; if you want to celebrate, dessert and the tip are a lovely touch but I can’t let you pick up more than that. Next time I’ll get the coffee or we can alternate—deal?
